# UnleeshAI: full text

UnleeshAI (wordmark UNLEESH) is a remote web design studio serving clients across the US. It designs and hand-codes custom websites and landing pages, then grows their visibility and conversion with SEO, AEO and AIO (also called GEO or AI SEO), content, and sales funnels.

## Service: Custom Website Design
URL: https://unleeshai.com/website-design.html
Pricing: From $499. Timeline: 2 to 4 days.

Custom website design means a site drawn and coded for your business alone, with no template underneath. Ours start at $499 for five pages and most go live in two to four days.

Custom website design is a website planned, designed and coded for one business, instead of a template with a new logo dropped in. At UNLEESH every site is hand-coded. A five-page website starts at $499, and most builds go live two to four days after we agree the brief, three on average.

The quiet fear with any new website is paying for something that looks fine and changes nothing. So we start from the job the site has to do: who needs to find it, what they need to believe, and what they should do next. The design follows from that, not the other way round.

### What you get

- A site designed around your offer and your buyer, not a theme chosen from a gallery

- Hand-written code: no page builder, no plugin stack, nothing to rent month after month

- Layouts that work on a phone first, then scale up to a desktop

- Search foundations from the first commit: page titles, descriptions, structured data, a sitemap and clean headings

- Pages structured so AI assistants can read and quote them, covered in AEO and AI SEO

- Motion and imagery where they earn their place, and a speed budget that holds on a two-year-old phone

- The code and the domain are yours when we are done

### How the build works

It starts with a short brief: what the business does, who you want to reach and what the site should get them to do. We reply with a fixed quote and a ship date. Day one is structure, copy and the visual direction. Day two is the home page in the browser, then the remaining pages. Day three is you looking at a working site instead of a mock-up, and telling us what to change before it goes live.

Because you see the real thing early, feedback is about the site and not about a slide of the site. That is most of why the timeline is days instead of weeks.

### What it costs

A five-page website starts at $499. Past that we do not guess. More pages, online booking, payments, a product catalogue, a members area or a content system all change the work, so we price them once we know what you need. The quote is fixed and in writing, and it does not move unless the scope does. The longer answer is in how much a website costs in 2026.

### Who it is for

Businesses whose current site undersells them, new businesses that need to look established from day one, and owners who are tired of a builder site that looks like everyone else's. If you only need one page for a campaign, a landing page is the better fit. If you already have a site you like and it is slow or invisible, look at website optimization or SEO instead.

You can see three live client builds and ten concept sites on the Work page.

### Common questions

Q: How much does a custom website cost?
A: A five-page custom website from UNLEESH starts at $499. Larger sites and sites with booking, payments or a catalogue are quoted at a fixed price once we know what needs building.

Q: How long does it take to build a website?
A: Two to four days from an agreed brief to launch, and three is the average. The exact ship date is written into your quote before any work starts.

Q: Do you use templates or page builders?
A: No. Every site is designed for the business and hand-coded. There is no template, no page builder and no plugin stack underneath, which is why the pages load fast and why you own the code.

Q: Will my website show up on Google?
A: The foundations are built in: titles, descriptions, structured data, a sitemap, fast pages and clear headings. Ranking for competitive searches takes ongoing work, which is what our SEO service covers.

Q: Do I own the website when it is finished?
A: Yes. The code and the domain are yours. You are not renting the site from us or from a platform.

## Service: Landing Page Design
URL: https://unleeshai.com/landing-page-design.html
Pricing: Fixed quote. Timeline: Set in the quote.

A landing page is a single page built around one offer and one action. We design and hand-code landing pages for ads, email campaigns and launches, with the form and the follow-up wired in.

A landing page is one page with one job: take a visitor who arrived from a specific place and get them to do one specific thing. We design and hand-code landing pages for ad campaigns, email campaigns, launches and lead magnets. Each one is built around a single offer, a single action and nothing that distracts from either.

If you are paying for clicks, the quiet fear is that the money is leaking somewhere between the ad and the enquiry. It usually is, and it usually leaks on the page. A home page asks visitors to find what they came for. A landing page hands it to them.

### What you get

- One page planned around one offer and one call to action

- A headline that matches the ad or email that sent the visitor, so the click feels continuous

- Proof placed where the doubt appears: reviews, numbers, guarantees, answers to objections

- A form, booking calendar or checkout that works on a phone with one thumb

- A thank-you step that tells people what happens next

- Tracking on the page so you can see how many visitors act, not only how many arrive

- Fast load times, because every second of delay costs paid traffic

### How we build it

We start with the offer, not the layout. What is being promised, to whom, and what would stop them saying yes. Then we plan the path from the first line to the button, and cut anything that does not move a visitor along it. Navigation, extra links and secondary offers all come out, because every extra link is a way to leave without acting.

The page is hand-coded, so there is no page-builder weight slowing it down. One of our live builds is exactly this kind of page: a single-offer landing page for an owner-financed land company, shown on the Work page.

### Pricing and timeline

A landing page is quoted at a fixed price once we know the offer, the copy you already have and what the form needs to connect to. For scale, a full five-page website starts at $499 and goes live in two to four days. The price and the ship date for your page are written into the quote before any work starts.

### Landing page or website?

You need a website when people are checking whether you are real. You need a landing page when you are sending traffic somewhere and want it to do one thing. Most businesses end up with both. The comparison is laid out in landing page vs website. When a landing page needs follow-up emails and a measured path behind it, that is a sales funnel.

### Common questions

Q: What is a landing page?
A: A landing page is a single web page built around one offer and one action, such as requesting a quote, booking a call or buying a product. Visitors usually arrive on it from an ad, an email or a social post.

Q: How is a landing page different from a home page?
A: A home page introduces the whole business and lets visitors explore. A landing page removes navigation and side offers on purpose so the visitor does one thing.

Q: Do I need a website before I get a landing page?
A: No. A landing page can stand alone for a campaign. A full website helps when people look you up before they buy, which is why most businesses end up with both.

Q: Can you write the copy for the page?
A: Yes. We write the headline, the offer and the body copy, or tighten what you already have. Copy is part of the build, not an extra.

## Service: SEO Services
URL: https://unleeshai.com/seo-services.html
Pricing: Fixed quote. Timeline: Months, not weeks.

SEO is the work that gets your website shown when people search for what you sell. We handle the technical fixes, the page-by-page optimization, local search and the content, and we report on enquiries, not vanity numbers.

SEO, or search engine optimization, is the work that gets your website shown when someone searches for what you sell. Our SEO service covers the technical foundations, on-page optimization, local search and the content that earns rankings. We quote each piece at a fixed price and we tell you up front that results take months, not weeks.

Most owners who ask about SEO have been burned once: a monthly fee, a report full of charts, and a phone that did not ring any more than before. So we report in the order that matters: impressions, then clicks, then enquiries. Enquiries are the only number that pays a bill.

### What the work includes

- A technical audit: crawl errors, broken links, slow pages, missing or duplicate titles, thin pages, mobile problems

- On-page optimization: titles, descriptions, headings, internal links and copy matched to what people actually search

- Structured data so search engines understand your business, services, prices and FAQs

- Local SEO: Google Business Profile, consistent name, address and phone details, local landing pages

- Keyword research built on buyer intent, not on the biggest number in a tool

- New pages and articles for the searches you should be winning, through blog writing

- Reporting from Google Search Console and analytics, in plain language

### How long SEO takes

Plan on months. Google's own guidance on hiring an SEO says to expect four months to a year before improvements are in place and the benefit shows. The first month is foundations. Months two and three are content. From month four the compounding starts: pages move from page three to page two to the bottom of page one. The month-by-month version is in how long SEO takes to work.

Two things shorten the wait. A fast, well-built site gives every page a better start. And specific searches move sooner than broad ones: a page about one service in one place will rank long before a page about an entire industry.

### Pricing

SEO is quoted at a fixed price for a defined piece of work: an audit, a set of pages to optimize, a local search setup, a month of content. You know the cost and the deliverable before anything starts. Ongoing work is quoted the same way: a defined month of deliverables, written down.

### SEO and AI search

More buyers now ask ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Google's AI Overviews instead of scrolling a results page. The two kinds of search reward much of the same work, and we build for both. The AI side is covered in AEO and AI SEO.

One of our live builds is a long-form page written to rank for owner-financed land searches in Florida. It is on the Work page.

### Common questions

Q: What is SEO?
A: SEO, or search engine optimization, is the practice of improving a website so it appears higher in search results when people look for what the business offers. It covers technical health, page content, local listings and links from other sites.

Q: How long does SEO take to work?
A: Usually months, not weeks. Google's own guidance says four months to a year. Impressions tend to move first, then clicks, then enquiries.

Q: How much does SEO cost?
A: We quote SEO at a fixed price for a defined piece of work, such as an audit, a set of pages or a month of content, once we have looked at your site and your market.

Q: Do you do SEO for websites you did not build?
A: Yes. We start with an audit of the existing site, fix what is holding it back and then build on it. If the site itself is the problem, we will say so.

Q: Is SEO still worth it now that people use AI?
A: Yes. AI assistants lean on pages that rank well and read clearly, so good SEO helps in both places. We treat AEO and AI SEO as part of the same job.

## Service: AEO and AI SEO
URL: https://unleeshai.com/aeo-ai-seo.html
Pricing: Fixed quote. Timeline: Weeks to months.

AEO is answer engine optimization: getting your business named when someone asks an AI assistant instead of a search engine. It is also called AIO, GEO or AI SEO. We build it into your site and your content.

AEO stands for answer engine optimization. It is the work of getting your business named, quoted or linked when someone asks ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini or Google's AI Overviews a question. You will also hear it called AIO (AI Overview optimization), GEO (generative engine optimization) or simply AI SEO. They describe the same job, and we do all of it.

The quiet fear is simple: a buyer asks an assistant who to hire, and the assistant names three of your competitors. Search engines hand out a list of ten. Answer engines hand out a recommendation of two or three. You want to be in the recommendation.

### What the work includes

- An AI visibility check: we ask the assistants the questions your buyers ask and record who gets named

- Structured data that states plainly who you are, what you sell, what it costs and where you work

- Pages rewritten to answer first: the direct answer in the opening lines, the detail after

- Question-style headings and FAQ sections that match the way people phrase prompts

- A check that AI crawlers are allowed in, and an llms.txt summary of the site

- Consistent facts across your site, Google Business Profile, directories and social profiles

- A plan for mentions you do not control: reviews, forums, local press and industry roundups

### How assistants decide who to name

An assistant recommends the business it can describe with confidence. That confidence comes from three places: a site it can read, facts that agree everywhere it looks, and other people vouching for you. Most assistants can also look things up on the live web when they answer, so a page that ranks well and reads clearly has a head start. That is why AEO sits on top of SEO instead of replacing it.

There is no form to submit and no placement to buy. What you can do is remove every reason an assistant might have to skip you. The full walk-through is in how to get your business recommended by ChatGPT, and the terms are untangled in AEO, GEO and AI SEO explained.

### How long it takes

Expect weeks to months. Assistants refresh what they know on their own schedule, and mentions on other sites take time to build. The on-site work, which is structure, answers and consistency, can be done quickly. We test the same set of questions on a regular schedule so you can see the change.

### Pricing

AEO is quoted at a fixed price for a defined piece of work: a visibility check, a set of pages restructured, a full site pass. When we build your site, the structural part is included from the first commit. See custom website design.

### Common questions

Q: What is AEO?
A: AEO is answer engine optimization: improving a website and its wider presence so AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews name or cite the business in their answers.

Q: Is AEO the same as GEO, AIO and AI SEO?
A: Largely, yes. GEO means generative engine optimization, AIO usually means AI Overview optimization, and AI SEO is the plain version. The work overlaps almost completely.

Q: Can you guarantee that ChatGPT will recommend my business?
A: No, and nobody honestly can. Assistants choose their own sources. What we can do is make your business easy to read, easy to verify and well vouched for, then measure the change.

Q: Does AEO replace SEO?
A: No. It sits on top of it. Pages that rank well and read clearly are the ones assistants tend to draw on, so the two are best done together.

Q: How do I check whether AI assistants mention my business?
A: Ask three assistants the questions your customers would ask before hiring someone like you, and write down who gets named. Repeat it monthly. We run this check at the start of every AEO project.

## Service: Sales Funnels
URL: https://unleeshai.com/sales-funnels.html
Pricing: Fixed quote. Timeline: Set in the quote.

A sales funnel is the path a stranger takes to become a customer, mapped out and built on purpose. We build the landing page, the capture, the thank-you step and the follow-up, and we measure every stage.

A sales funnel is the path a stranger takes to become a customer, mapped out and built on purpose. In practice it is a short chain: something that brings the right people in, a page that makes one offer, a way to act on it, and follow-up for the people who are not ready yet. We design and build that chain and we measure each link.

Every business already has a funnel. Most were built by accident: someone hears about you, searches your name, lands on a home page, hunts for a phone number and maybe calls. Each step loses people. The quiet fear is not knowing which step, and the honest answer is that without measurement nobody knows.

### What we build

- The offer: what a visitor gets in exchange for a click, an email address or a call

- A landing page built around that one offer

- The capture: a form, a booking calendar or a checkout that works on a phone

- A thank-you step that sets the next action instead of ending the conversation

- A short follow-up sequence that answers the questions people have before they buy

- Tracking at every stage, so the biggest drop is visible

### The offer matters more than the pages

A beautiful page with a weak offer converts worse than a plain page with a strong one. So we start by pressure-testing the offer: is it worth an email address, is it clear in one sentence, does it match what the ad or the search promised. Only then do we draw anything.

### Follow-up is where the money is

Few people buy on the first visit. A funnel without follow-up pays to attract visitors and then lets nearly all of them leave with no way to reach them again. Three or four honest emails that answer real objections will often do more than another month of ad spend.

### Measuring it

Four numbers, tracked separately: how many people arrive, how many act on the offer, how many respond to follow-up, how many become customers. The step with the biggest drop gets fixed first. Without those four numbers every change is a guess.

### Pricing

A funnel is quoted at a fixed price once we know the offer, the number of steps and what the capture has to connect to, such as your CRM, your calendar or your email tool. Getting visitors into the top of it is covered in traffic generation. The plain-words explainer is what a sales funnel is.

### Common questions

Q: What is a sales funnel?
A: A sales funnel is the sequence of steps that turns a stranger into a customer: attention, an offer, a way to act on it, and follow-up. Building one on purpose means each step can be measured and improved.

Q: Does a small business need a sales funnel?
A: Yes, because it already has one. The question is whether it was designed or happened by accident. A simple funnel with a clear offer, a working form and a few follow-up messages is enough for most small businesses.

Q: What is the difference between a landing page and a sales funnel?
A: A landing page is one page. A funnel is the whole path: the landing page, the capture, the thank-you step and the follow-up that comes after.

Q: Do I need special funnel software?
A: No. You need a page with one clear offer, a form that works and a way to send follow-up messages. We build the pages and wire them to the tools you already use.

## Service: Blog Writing Services
URL: https://unleeshai.com/blog-writing.html
Pricing: Fixed quote. Timeline: Set in the quote.

Blog writing that answers the questions your buyers actually type. Each article is planned around a real search, opens with the direct answer, and is structured to rank on Google and be quoted by AI assistants.

Our blog writing service produces articles that answer the questions your buyers actually type into Google and ask AI assistants. Each piece is planned around a real search, opens with the direct answer and is structured so it can rank and be quoted. It reads like a person talking, not like a brochure.

Most business blogs are a graveyard: six posts from two years ago about company news nobody searched for. The quiet fear is spending money on more of the same. The fix is to stop writing about yourself and start answering questions.

### What you get

- Topic research: the questions your buyers ask, ranked by how likely the asker is to buy

- A title written as the question, because that is how people search and how they prompt

- The direct answer in the first two sentences, then the detail

- Clear subheadings every few paragraphs, so readers and machines can both find their place

- Internal links to the service or product the article supports

- A page title, description and structured data for every article

- Your voice, your facts and no invented statistics

### How we choose topics

We start with cost, time and comparison questions, because the people asking them are close to buying. How much does it cost. How long does it take. Which option is right for me. Is it worth it. An article that answers one of those clearly will do more than ten posts of general advice.

Then we look at what already ranks and what the AI assistants say when asked the same question. If the existing answers are vague, there is room. If they are excellent, we pick a narrower question you can own.

### Written for search and for AI answers

The structure that helps an article rank is the same structure that makes it quotable: a question as the heading, the answer straight after it, short paragraphs and consistent facts. That is the content half of SEO and of AEO and AI SEO.

You can read our own in the Journal. Entries such as how much a website costs and how long SEO takes follow exactly this pattern.

### Pricing

Blog writing is quoted at a fixed price for a set number of articles, with the topics agreed first. You see the list before anything is written.

### Common questions

Q: What does a blog writing service include?
A: Topic research, a title built around a real search, the article itself with clear subheadings, internal links, and the page title, description and structured data that go with it.

Q: How does blog writing help SEO?
A: Each article is a new page that can rank for a specific question, and it links readers to the service it supports. Over time a set of focused articles brings in searches a small site could never win with service pages alone.

Q: How long should a blog post be?
A: As long as the question needs. A cost or how-to question usually takes 800 to 1,500 words to answer properly. Padding does not help. Completeness does.

Q: Who chooses the topics?
A: We propose a list based on the questions your buyers search for and ask AI assistants, and you approve it before anything is written. Nothing is published with invented statistics.

## Service: Website Optimization
URL: https://unleeshai.com/website-optimization.html
Pricing: Fixed quote. Timeline: Set in the quote.

Website optimization makes the site you already have faster, easier to use and better at turning visitors into enquiries. We audit it, fix what is slowing it down or losing people, and measure the difference.

Website optimization is the work of making an existing website faster, easier to use and better at turning visitors into enquiries. We audit the site, fix what is slowing it down or losing people, and measure the before and after. You keep the site you have. It just starts doing its job.

The quiet fear here is that the whole site needs rebuilding. Sometimes it does, and we will say so. More often a handful of problems account for most of the damage: images several times larger than they need to be, scripts that block the page from showing, a form that is painful on a phone.

### What we look at

- Load speed on a real phone on a mobile connection, not only on a desktop

- Core Web Vitals, the three measurements Google uses for loading, responsiveness and visual stability

- Images, video and fonts: size, format and how they load

- Scripts and plugins that are slowing every page for the sake of one feature

- The path to enquiry: how many taps it takes to call, book or buy

- Forms: fields nobody needs, errors nobody can read, buttons too small to press

- Search basics that are missing: titles, descriptions, headings, structured data

### Speed

A slow page loses visitors before they see anything. It also costs you in search, because page experience is one of the things Google measures. Most speed problems come from weight, meaning too much being sent to the browser, and from order, meaning the wrong things being sent first. We reduce the first and fix the second.

### Conversion

A fast page that confuses people still loses them. So the second half of the work is the path: is it obvious what you sell, is the next step visible without scrolling on a phone, does the form ask for only what you need. Small changes here often matter more than a redesign.

### Audit first, then a fixed quote

We start with an audit and give you a written list of what we found, ordered by how much each fix is likely to help. Then we quote the fixes at a fixed price. You can take the whole list, or the top three.

### When a rebuild is the better answer

If the site sits on a platform that cannot be made fast, or the structure fights every fix, patching costs more than starting clean. A custom five-page site starts at $499 and goes live in two to four days. See custom website design. Once the site is quick, SEO and traffic generation have something worth sending people to.

### Common questions

Q: What is website optimization?
A: Website optimization is improving an existing site so it loads faster, is easier to use and converts more visitors into enquiries or sales. It covers speed, Core Web Vitals, mobile usability, forms and the path to contact.

Q: How do I know if my website is slow?
A: Open it on your phone using mobile data, not wifi. If you are waiting more than a couple of seconds to see the page, so are your visitors. Google's free PageSpeed Insights tool will give you the measurements.

Q: What are Core Web Vitals?
A: Core Web Vitals are three measurements Google uses to judge page experience: how quickly the main content loads, how quickly the page responds when you tap, and how much the layout shifts while loading.

Q: Should I optimize my site or rebuild it?
A: Optimize when the problems are specific and fixable, such as heavy images or blocking scripts. Rebuild when the platform or structure fights every fix. Our audit tells you which case you are in.

## Service: Traffic Generation
URL: https://unleeshai.com/traffic-generation.html
Pricing: Fixed quote. Timeline: Depends on the channel.

Traffic generation is the work of bringing the right visitors to your website: people who are looking for what you sell. We combine search, content, AI answers, email and campaigns, and point them at pages built to convert.

Traffic generation is the work of bringing the right visitors to your website, meaning people who are already looking for what you sell. We combine search, content, AI answers, email and paid campaigns, and we point all of it at pages built to turn a visit into an enquiry.

A website with no visitors is an expensive secret. The quiet fear is the opposite problem: paying for traffic and watching it bounce. So we treat traffic and conversion as one job. There is no point filling a leaky bucket faster.

### Where the traffic comes from

- Search: pages and articles that rank for what your buyers type, through SEO

- AI answers: being named by ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews, through AEO and AI SEO

- Content: articles that answer buying questions, through blog writing

- Email: campaigns to the list you already have, and outreach to the people you want to reach

- Paid campaigns: search and social ads sent to a dedicated landing page

- Local: your Google Business Profile, maps and directories, for businesses that serve an area

### Fast channels and slow channels

Paid ads and email can bring visitors within days, and they stop when you stop. Search and content take months to build, and they keep working after the work is done. A sensible plan uses a fast channel to bring enquiries now and a slow channel to lower the cost of every enquiry later.

### Right visitors, not more visitors

Ten visitors who are ready to buy are worth more than a thousand who are browsing. We choose channels and keywords by intent: what the person was trying to do when they found you. Traffic numbers are easy to inflate. Enquiries are not.

### Where the traffic lands

Every campaign points at a page built for it. Ad traffic goes to a landing page that repeats the promise in the ad. Search traffic goes to the page that answers the search. When the landing page has follow-up behind it, that is a sales funnel. If the site itself is slow or confusing, we fix that first through website optimization.

### Pricing

We quote the work at a fixed price once we know which channels fit your business: a campaign set up, a set of pages, a month of content. Any ad spend is paid by you directly to the platform, and it is separate from our fee.

### Common questions

Q: What is traffic generation?
A: Traffic generation is the work of bringing visitors to a website through channels such as search, content, AI answers, email, social media and paid ads. Done well, it brings people who are already looking for what the business sells.

Q: What is the fastest way to get traffic to a website?
A: Paid ads and email are the fastest, often within days. They stop when the spend stops. Search and content are slower to start and keep bringing visitors long after the work is done.

Q: How long does it take to get organic traffic?
A: Usually months. Google's own guidance on SEO says four months to a year. Specific, low-competition searches can move sooner than broad ones.

Q: Why is my website getting traffic but no enquiries?
A: Usually one of three reasons: the visitors are the wrong people, the page does not match what they were promised, or the next step is hard to find or hard to complete. We check all three before recommending more traffic.

## Case study: Lumen Skincare (Beauty Flagship, studio concept)
URL: https://unleeshai.com/work_lumen.html

Redefining clean beauty: a bespoke digital experience blending editorial layouts with an organic palette.

Concept: The concept carries the full line on a single scroll: ingredient stories, ritual pages and a checkout that never breaks the calm. Every product frame was generated under the same key light, so the catalogue reads as one shoot.

Scope explored: Brand Audit, Premium UI/UX, Product Site. Proposed stack: GSAP · Lenis · Shopify Hydrogen.

## Case study: Pull Noodle Bar (F&B Retail, studio concept)
URL: https://unleeshai.com/work_pullnoodle.html

Hand-pulled craft caught mid-air: flour dust in a single shaft of light.

Premise: Imagine a noodle house with a queue around the block, and a site that moves like the kitchen: fast, precise, theatrical.

Concept: In the concept, ordering is three taps and one animation. The menu plays as a single kitchen sequence, and a queue page tells waiting guests how long until their bowl.

Scope explored: Brand Core, Ordering UX, AI Visual Showcase. Proposed stack: GSAP · Lenis · PWA.

URL: https://unleeshai.com/work_axiom.html

CNC tolerances as brand language: titanium, coolant spray and sparks of white light.

Premise: Imagine a machining firm that needs to prove precision. We answered with macro frames of the work itself, down to the tool marks.

Concept: Capabilities are shown, not claimed: every process page opens on the machine at work. The quote flow is designed to read a CAD upload and return a scoped estimate in the same session.

Foundry glow as the only colour in a monochrome world.

## How much does a website cost in 2026?
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_how-much-does-a-website-cost.html
Published: 2026-11-16 · Strategy

The honest answer is a range so wide it is useless, until you know the five things that move the price. Here they are, with our own number on the table.

A website in 2026 can cost nothing, or it can cost more than a car. A free builder page, a freelancer, a studio and a large agency will all sell you something called a website, and the prices climb steeply at each step. Our own number, so you have one real figure to hold on to: a custom five-page website from UNLEESH starts at $499. The rest of this entry explains why quotes vary so much and how to tell which price is right for you.

### What decides the price of a website?

Five things move the price. Page count is the obvious one. The second is whether the design is custom or a template with your logo dropped in. The third is content: who writes the words and where the images come from. The fourth is function, meaning anything the site has to do beyond being read, such as booking, payments, logins or a product catalogue. The fifth is what happens after launch: search optimization, content and upkeep. Most surprise invoices come from numbers three and five, because nobody priced them at the start.

### What do the common options cost you?

The cheapest route is a do-it-yourself builder. It costs a monthly fee and your own evenings. That is a fair trade for a brand-new business that needs to exist online this week. The hidden cost shows up later: a template that looks like a thousand other sites, pages that load slowly, and a platform you rent rather than own.

A freelancer sits between the builder and the agency. You get one person's skill and one person's availability. That works well when the person is good and stays reachable. Ask who maintains the site if they move on, and whether you will hold the logins.

The most expensive route is a large agency. You are paying for account managers, discovery workshops and a process built for companies with a marketing department. If you have one, that process is worth it. If you are an owner who needs a site that brings in enquiries, you are mostly paying for meetings.

The middle is where most small businesses should shop, and it is where the quality varies most. Ask three questions of any quote. Is the price fixed, or an estimate? Do I own the code and the domain when it is done? And what exactly is included for search: page titles, structured data, speed, a sitemap, or nothing? A site nobody can find is the most expensive kind, whatever the invoice says.

### What are the costs nobody mentions?

Four costs sit outside most quotes. A domain name, renewed every year. Hosting, paid monthly or yearly. Email on your own domain. And changes after launch: new pages, new photos, a new offer. None of them is large. All of them are easier to plan for when they are written down at the start. Ask every provider which of the four are in the price and which are not.

### How do we price a website?

Here is how we price. A five-page site starts at $499. Past that we do not guess: once we know what needs building, we quote a fixed price, and it does not move unless the scope does. Most of our builds are live in two to four days from an agreed brief. Search foundations are built in from the first commit instead of sold as an extra after launch.

The full scope of what is included is on the custom website design page.

### How do you know what you should pay?

A cheap website is not the one with the lowest invoice. It is the one that pays for itself fastest. Price the site against what one new customer is worth to you, then ask how many customers it needs to bring in to cover its cost. If the answer is one or two, the decision is easier than it looked.

Then compare quotes on the same five lines: page count, custom or template, who writes the copy, what the site has to do, and what happens after launch. Two quotes that look far apart often turn out to be pricing different jobs. The useful question is not which is cheaper. It is which one includes the things that make the site earn its keep.

### Quick answers

Can you get a website for free?

Yes, on a builder's free plan, usually with the builder's branding and web address instead of your own. It is fine for testing an idea. It is a weak first impression for a business asking people to pay.

Is a $499 website any good?

It depends what the $499 buys. Ours buys five custom, hand-coded pages with search foundations built in. The price is low because the build takes days instead of weeks, not because corners are cut.

What should a small business budget for a website?

Budget for the build, then for the four running costs above, then for the work that gets the site found. A site with no plan for search or content tends to sit unvisited, whatever it cost to make.

## What is AEO? AEO, GEO and AI SEO explained in plain words
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_what-is-aeo-geo-ai-seo.html
Published: 2026-11-16 · Search

Four acronyms, one job: getting your business named when someone asks an AI assistant instead of a search engine. Here is what the work actually is.

AEO stands for answer engine optimization. It is the work of getting your business named, quoted or linked when someone asks an AI assistant a question instead of typing it into a search box. The assistants in question are ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and the AI Overviews that now sit at the top of many Google results.

### Is AEO the same as GEO, AIO and AI SEO?

You will hear the same job called by other names. GEO means generative engine optimization. AIO usually means AI Overview optimization, or simply AI optimization. AI SEO and AI search optimization are the plain versions. They overlap almost completely. We say AEO and AIO because those are the terms our clients arrive with, but if an agency sells you GEO, it is describing the same work.

### How is AEO different from SEO?

The difference from classic SEO is the shape of the result. Search engines hand out a list. Answer engines hand out a recommendation. On a results page you can win a click from position four. In an AI answer there is often no position four: the assistant names two or three businesses and the conversation moves on.

AEO does not replace SEO. It sits on top of it. Most assistants can look things up on the live web when they answer, so a page that ranks well and reads clearly has a head start. That is why we build both into a site from the first commit instead of treating AI search as a separate project.

### What does AEO work actually involve?

So what does the work look like? First, the site has to be readable by machines: clean HTML, fast pages, and structured data that says plainly who you are, what you sell and where you work. Second, the content has to answer real questions directly. A page that opens with a clear answer in its first two sentences is easy to quote. A page that opens with three paragraphs of mood is not.

Third, the facts about your business have to match everywhere they appear: your site, your Google Business Profile, directories, review sites and social profiles. An assistant that finds three different descriptions of what you do will trust none of them. Fourth, other people need to mention you. Reviews, forum threads, local press and industry roundups all count, because assistants lean on what the wider web says about a business, not only on what the business says about itself.

### Which AI assistants matter?

The ones your buyers already use. ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini are asked directly. Google's AI Overviews appear above ordinary search results, so people meet them without choosing to. Each one gathers information a little differently, but they reward the same things: a site they can read, facts that agree, and other sources that vouch for you. You do not need a separate plan for each.

### How long does AEO take to work?

Longer than a site edit and shorter than most people fear. The on-site work, meaning structure, direct answers and consistent facts, can be done in days. The off-site part, meaning reviews and mentions, builds over weeks and months. Assistants also refresh what they know on their own schedule, so a change you make today may take a while to show up in an answer.

### What does AEO not do?

It does not buy a placement, because there is none for sale. It does not guarantee a mention, because the assistant chooses its own sources. And it does not rescue a business with nothing to say. An assistant can only repeat what it can find, so the work starts with having clear, specific, true things published about what you do.

### Where do you start?

Start with the three pages that matter most: your home page, your main service page and your contact page. Make sure each one says in its first lines what you do, who for and where. Add the questions buyers ask, with short direct answers. Check that your business name, services and location read the same on your Google Business Profile. For most small businesses that is about a week of work, and it covers most of the ground.

### How can you check your own AI visibility?

A quick test you can run today: open two or three assistants and ask the question your best customer would ask before hiring someone like you. Note who gets named. If it is not you, read what those businesses publish and where they are mentioned. That gap is the work.

If you would rather hand the work over, this is what our AEO and AI SEO service covers.

## How do you get your business recommended by ChatGPT?
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_get-recommended-by-chatgpt.html
Published: 2026-11-16 · Search

You cannot pay for it and you cannot trick it. You can make your business easy to find, easy to understand and easy to vouch for.

You get recommended by ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Gemini the same way you get recommended by a well-informed friend: by being easy to find, easy to understand and vouched for by other people. There is no form to submit and no placement to buy. What you can do is remove every reason an assistant might have to skip you.

### Can an AI assistant understand what you do?

Start with being understood. An assistant recommends the business it can describe with confidence. Your site should state in plain sentences what you do, who you do it for, where you work and what it costs or how pricing works. If a stranger cannot summarise your business after reading your home page for ten seconds, neither can a machine.

### Can it read your website?

Then make the site readable. That means fast pages, real text instead of words baked into images, a clear heading on every page, and structured data that labels your business, services and frequently asked questions. Check that your site is not blocking AI crawlers by accident. Some are, through a security setting nobody remembers switching on.

### Do you answer the questions buyers ask?

Answer the questions buyers actually ask. Assistants are asked things like how much a service costs, how long it takes, and who is good at it in a given city or industry. A page that answers one of those directly, in its opening lines, is far more quotable than a page of slogans. Question-style headings help, because they match the way people phrase prompts.

### Who else vouches for you?

Get mentioned in places you do not control. Reviews on Google and industry platforms, answers on Reddit and Quora, local news, supplier and partner pages, podcast notes. Assistants weigh what the wider web says about you more heavily than what you say about yourself, in the same way a person would.

### Do your facts agree everywhere?

Keep the facts consistent. Name, services, location, hours and pricing should read the same on your site, your Google Business Profile, your social profiles and every directory. Conflicting details make an assistant hedge, and a hedged answer usually names someone else.

### Does being on Google still matter?

Yes. Most assistants can search the live web when they answer, and they lean on pages that already rank and read clearly. A business that is invisible on Google is usually invisible to assistants too. Treat search and AI answers as one job with two outputs.

### What does not work?

Stuffing a page with keywords does not work. Neither does hiding text, publishing dozens of thin pages, or writing copy addressed to the machine instead of the reader. Assistants are built to summarise what a careful reader would take from a page. Anything a careful reader would find odd, an assistant tends to discount.

### A one-week checklist

- Write one sentence that says what you do, who for and where, and put it at the top of your home page

- Give each service its own page or section, with the price or how pricing works

- Add the five questions buyers ask most, each with a two-sentence answer

- Check that your name, services, hours and location match on your site and your Google Business Profile

- Ask three recent customers for a review

- Ask three assistants who they would recommend for what you do, and write down the answer

### How long until it changes?

Then test it. Once a month, ask three assistants the questions your customers ask and write down who gets named. It will not change overnight. Assistants refresh what they know on their own schedule, so expect weeks to months. The businesses that show up a year from now are the ones that started tidying up today.

We do this for clients as part of AEO and AI SEO.

## How long does SEO take to work?
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_how-long-does-seo-take.html
Published: 2026-11-16 · Search

Months, not weeks. Here is what happens in each of them, and how to tell real progress from a nice-looking report.

SEO usually takes months, not weeks, to show results you can feel in the business. Google's own guidance on hiring an SEO says to expect four months to a year before improvements are in place and the benefit shows. A brand-new domain sits at the slow end of that range. An established site with fixable problems can move faster.

### Why does SEO take so long?

It is slow for a reason. A search engine has to crawl your pages, understand them, compare them with every other page on the subject, and watch how people respond. Trust is earned through consistency, and consistency takes time to observe. SEO is slow for the same reason it is valuable: you cannot buy your way to the front of it overnight.

### What happens in the first month?

The first month is foundations. Fix what stops pages being crawled and understood: broken links, slow loading, missing titles, thin or duplicate pages, no structured data. None of this is visible to a visitor, and all of it decides whether the rest of the work counts.

### What happens in months two and three?

Months two and three are content. Each service gets a page that says clearly what it is, who it is for and what it costs or how it is priced. Questions customers actually ask get direct answers. This is when impressions start to climb in Google Search Console, usually well before clicks do.

### When do results start to show?

From month four onward the compounding starts. Pages that were on page three move to page two, then to the bottom of page one. Clicks follow rankings, and enquiries follow clicks. New content builds on pages that already have some standing instead of starting from zero.

### How do you tell real progress from a nice report?

How do you tell real progress from a nice-looking report? Look at three numbers in this order: impressions, then clicks, then enquiries. Impressions rising means Google is showing you for more searches. Clicks rising means the right people are choosing you. Enquiries rising is the only number that pays a bill, and any report that never mentions it is hiding something.

### What makes SEO faster?

Two things shorten the wait. A fast, well-built site gives every page a better start, which is why we build search foundations in from the first commit. And choosing specific searches over broad ones gets results sooner: a page about owner-financed land in Florida will rank long before a page about real estate.

A third thing helps: fixing what is already there before publishing anything new. A site with twenty weak pages improves faster by repairing the five that matter than by adding twenty more.

### What slows SEO down?

A brand-new domain with no history. A crowded market where every competitor has been at it for years. A site that changes address or structure halfway through. And stopping: rankings earned over six months can fade if the work stops while competitors carry on.

### Can you get results sooner?

For some searches, yes. Your own business name should show within days of the site being indexed. Very specific local searches can move within weeks. If you need enquiries this month, a paid campaign pointed at a landing page will bring them while the slower work builds underneath.

What the work includes, piece by piece, is on our SEO services page.

## Landing page vs website: which one do you need?
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_landing-page-vs-website.html
Published: 2026-11-16 · Strategy

A website introduces the whole business. A landing page asks for one thing. Knowing which job you are hiring for saves money either way.

A website is the full picture of a business: what it does, who is behind it, the services, the proof and a way to get in touch. A landing page is a single page built around one offer and one action. You need a website when people are checking whether you are real. You need a landing page when you are sending traffic somewhere and want it to do one thing.

### What is the difference?

The difference is focus. A website answers every question. A landing page asks one. A good website has navigation, several pages and room to explore. A good landing page removes almost all of that on purpose, because every extra link is a way to leave without acting.

### When do you need a landing page?

Use a landing page when the visitor arrives from a specific place with a specific intent: an ad, an email, a social post, a QR code on a flyer. Someone who clicked an ad for a free quote should land on a page about that free quote, not on a home page where they have to find it again.

### When do you need a website?

Use a website when the visitor arrives without a script. People who search your business name, follow a referral or find you through a blog post want to look around before they trust you. A single page with one button feels thin to someone still deciding whether you are legitimate.

### Do you need both?

Most businesses end up needing both, in that order. The website comes first because it is what search engines and AI assistants read to understand who you are. Landing pages come second, one per campaign or offer, and they borrow the trust the main site has already earned.

### Where does a sales funnel fit?

A sales funnel is what you get when you connect them: a landing page that makes the offer, a form or checkout that captures the action, a thank-you page that sets the next step, and follow-up emails for the people who were not ready. The landing page is the front door of the funnel, not the whole building.

### What should a landing page include?

- A headline that matches the ad, email or post that sent the visitor

- The offer, stated in one sentence

- Proof next to the claim it supports: a review, a number, a guarantee

- One form or one button, repeated down the page

- No menu and no links that lead away

- A thank-you step that says what happens next

### What are the common mistakes?

Sending ad traffic to a home page is the most common one. The second is a landing page with three different buttons, which is a home page in disguise. The third is asking for too much: a ten-field form on a first visit loses people who would have given a name and an email.

### Which one should you build first?

If the budget only stretches to one, ask where your next ten customers will come from. If the answer is search and referrals, build the website. If the answer is ads or outreach you are about to switch on, build the landing page and point everything at it.

We build both: see landing page design and custom website design.

## What is a sales funnel, and does a small business need one?
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_what-is-a-sales-funnel.html
Published: 2026-11-16 · Strategy

A funnel is the path from stranger to customer, written down and built on purpose. You already have one. The question is whether it leaks.

A sales funnel is the path a stranger takes to become a customer, mapped out and built on purpose. In practice it is a short chain of pages and messages: something that gets attention, a page that makes one offer, a way to act on it, and follow-up for the people who are not ready yet. Yes, a small business needs one, because it already has one. Every business has a funnel. Most of them were built by accident.

### What does an accidental funnel look like?

The accidental version looks like this. Someone hears about you, searches your name, lands on a home page, hunts for a phone number, and maybe calls. Each of those steps loses people. A funnel is what you get when you look at each step and ask what would stop someone here.

### What are the parts of a simple funnel?

A simple funnel has four parts. Traffic: search, ads, social posts or referrals that bring the right people in. A landing page: one offer, one action, no distractions. A capture: a form, a booking calendar or a checkout. And follow-up: an email or message sequence that answers the questions people have before they buy.

### Why does the offer matter most?

The offer matters more than the pages. A free quote, a guide, a consultation, a first-order discount: whatever it is, it has to be worth giving an email address or a phone number for. A beautiful page with a weak offer converts worse than a plain page with a strong one.

### Why is follow-up where the money is?

Follow-up is where most of the money is. Few people buy on the first visit. A funnel without follow-up pays to attract visitors and then lets nearly all of them leave with no way to reach them again. Three or four honest emails that answer real objections will often do more than another month of ad spend.

### How do you measure a funnel?

Measure each step separately. How many people arrive, how many act on the offer, how many respond to follow-up, how many become customers. The step with the biggest drop is the one to fix first. Without those four numbers, every change is a guess.

### What does a small-business funnel look like?

Take a home services company. An ad offers a free quote for one specific job. The landing page repeats that offer and asks for a name, a phone number and a postcode. The thank-you page says when to expect a call. Two emails follow for anyone who does not pick up: one explaining what the job usually involves, one answering what past customers asked first. Four steps, and each one can be measured.

### Do you need funnel software?

You do not need software with funnel in the name to do any of this. You need a page that makes one clear offer, a form that works, and a short sequence of follow-up messages. We build the pages and wire the path, and we would rather you had a simple funnel that gets measured than an elaborate one that does not.

The pages, the capture and the follow-up are what our sales funnels service builds.

## Why your hero section is costing you clients
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_hero-section-costing-clients.html
Published: 2026-08-18 · Web Design

The first viewport is a job interview that lasts three seconds. Most premium brands fail it by saying everything at once.

Open ten agency sites in ten tabs and read only the first viewport. You will find the same sentence wearing different fonts: we craft digital experiences that drive results. Nobody hired anyone because of that sentence. It exists because a committee could not agree on what to leave out, so it left nothing out.

A hero is not a summary of the company. It is a single decision about what the visitor should feel first. On a fine-dining site that feeling is patience; on a machining site it is precision; on a skincare flagship it is calm. Once the feeling is chosen, the hero needs one image or loop that produces it, one line of type that names it, and a way down. Everything else belongs further down the page where the visitor has already decided to stay.

The cost of getting this wrong is measurable. Picture a B2B hero where the headline, a stat ticker, a video, a client logo strip and two buttons all compete for the same second. Paid traffic lands, finds nothing to hold on to, and leaves before the first scroll. Remove four of the six elements and the page finally says one thing, without a dollar more in ad spend.

The uncomfortable part is that the fix requires someone to be wrong. The stat ticker was somebody's idea. The logo strip was a sales request. Subtraction is a political act inside a company, which is why it is worth paying an outside studio to perform it.

## One key light: the whole aesthetic explained
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_one-key-light.html
Published: 2026-08-02 · AI Visuals

Every image we ship is lit from one direction. Here is why that single constraint does most of the work.

Ask a cinematographer what makes a frame feel expensive and they will not talk about the camera. They will talk about where the light comes from, how hard it is, and what it refuses to touch. Most product imagery on the web is lit from everywhere, because that is what a white studio and a ring light do. It looks clean and it looks like nothing.

Our rule is one key light, always slightly above and to the side, with a long falloff into near-black. Every still and every loop on this site obeys it. When a reference breaks the rule, we make both versions and put them side by side. The one-light version wins because it looks like it belongs with the rest of the brand, even when the rest of the brand does not exist yet.

The constraint matters even more for generated imagery. A diffusion model will happily give you forty product shots with forty different suns. Describing the light in words, in every prompt, is the difference between a catalogue and a pile of pictures. We write the light before we write the product.

Consistency is not a style. It is the absence of accidents. One key light removes the accidents so that the actual decisions, the material, the angle, the negative space, have room to be seen.

## AI product photography that passes for a five-figure shoot
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_ai-product-photography-five-figure-shoot.html
Published: 2026-07-22 · AI Visuals

Generated imagery is only cheap if you accept the first result. The craft is in the second, third and fourteenth.

The usual question about generated product imagery is why one frame looks like a stock photo and another looks like a campaign. The honest answer is that we threw away twenty frames to keep one, and we knew what we were looking for before we started.

A commercial shoot has a brief, a lighting plan, a shot list and an art director on set who says no. Generation removes the set and the crew but not the need for the other four. Our prompts read like lighting plans: the key light, the surface, the exact distance from lens to object, what stays out of frame. The model gives you a draft. The art director gives you a shoot.

Then there is the part nobody mentions: the retouch. Generated frames arrive with wrong reflections, invented text and lens behaviour that no lens has. Every client frame gets cleaned at pixel level before it ships. A keycap with a legible, real character on it is worth more than a hundred with alphabet soup.

The result is imagery that survives being placed next to real photography, which is the only test that matters. When a client cannot tell which frames were shot and which were generated, we have done the job.

## Scroll is a story, not a scrollbar
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_scroll-is-a-story.html
Published: 2026-07-10 · Motion

Scroll-driven motion earns its place when it changes what the reader understands, not just what they see.

Pinned sections, scrubbed timelines and parallax have become a dialect. Used badly, they turn a page into a theme park ride where every element must be endured before the content appears. Used well, they let the page control pace the way an editor controls a cut.

Our test for every scroll-driven beat is simple: does the reader know something at the end of it that they did not know at the start? A cube that assembles from six faces while six capabilities light up teaches the structure of the studio. A word that bounces because it can teaches nothing. If the animation can be removed without losing meaning, remove it.

The second test is reversibility. Anything the reader scrolls into, they will scroll out of. If the piece only works forward, it is a video, not an interaction. Every scrubbed tween on this site plays backwards cleanly, which is a discipline that costs time and pays back in trust.

The third test is the one most sites fail: the page must still read as a page. Motion is punctuation. When every sentence ends in an exclamation mark, the reader stops hearing any of them.

## The case against page builders for premium brands
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_case-against-page-builders.html
Published: 2026-06-28 · Strategy

A template is a decision someone else made about how your brand should feel. For most businesses that is fine. For a premium brand it is the whole problem.

Page builders solved a real problem: most businesses need a website, and a custom build used to cost more than they could justify. We are not arguing with that. We are arguing with the premium skincare house, the boutique clinic, the machining firm charging for tolerances no competitor can hit, when they ship a site that shares a skeleton with a dropshipping store.

You cannot charge a premium for a product that arrives in the same box as everyone else's. Visitors do not consciously recognise the template, but they recognise the rhythm: the hero, the three-column features, the testimonial slider, the footer. It reads as generic before a single word is processed, and generic is the opposite of what a premium price is asking the customer to believe.

There is a technical cost too. Builders ship megabytes of code to support features you did not use, and every animation runs through three layers of abstraction. The result is a site that is slower than it looks and harder to change than it should be. The debt arrives at the worst moment, usually a rebrand.

A hand-coded site is not a luxury. It is the only way to make the page do exactly one thing, feel exactly one way, and load exactly as fast as it should. For a brand that sells on precision, anything less is a contradiction on the front door.

## Motion tokens: a design system for time
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_motion-tokens.html
Published: 2026-06-15 · Motion

Colour and type have tokens. Motion should too. Here is the small set of durations and curves that runs every page we build.

A design system without motion tokens is a design system that stops at the edge of the static comp. The moment something moves, every developer invents their own timing and the brand fractures into a hundred slightly different bounces.

Our set is small on purpose. Four durations: fast for hover, base for reveals, slow for large surfaces, and a curtain length for full-screen transitions. Three curves: an expo-out for things arriving, an in-out for things travelling, and a soft ease for anything the reader is meant to ignore. One rule sits above all of it: every change eases, nothing snaps.

The tokens live in CSS custom properties and are read by GSAP, so a hover underline and a pinned scene share the same vocabulary. Changing the feel of an entire site becomes a two-line edit. That is what a system is for.

The payoff is not that the site moves more. It is that the site moves the same way everywhere, which the reader experiences as confidence. Nothing on the page feels improvised, because nothing was.

## Dark mode is not a theme, it is a stage
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_dark-mode-is-a-stage.html
Published: 2026-06-01 · Web Design

Designing on near-black is not inverting a light site. It is deciding that the content is the only thing lit.

Most dark modes are light modes with the values flipped. The same grid, the same card borders, the same drop shadows now pointing nowhere. The result is a site that looks like it is wearing sunglasses indoors.

A true dark design starts from a stage, not a page. The background is not a colour; it is the absence of light. Anything that appears is lit deliberately, and anything unlit does not exist. On a dark stage the light is the layout: the image with the single key light, the paragraph in soft white, the one hairline that separates two thoughts.

This changes small decisions. Cards lose their borders because a border is a lit edge with nothing behind it. Text goes one step brighter than instinct suggests, because grey on black reads as dust, not hierarchy. Video plates run at a third of their brightness so the type in front of them stays legible.

The reward is that the content gets to be the only bright thing in the room. That is a kind of attention a light background can never give it.

## What a brand audit actually finds (and what it costs to skip one)
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_brand-audit-findings.html
Published: 2026-05-20 · Strategy

Every project we take on begins with looking before making. The temptation is always to skip it. Here is what gets skipped.

An audit is time spent reading everything the brand has ever published: the site, the decks, the packaging, the support emails, the LinkedIn posts written at 11pm. We are not looking for mistakes. We are looking for the place where the brand tells the truth by accident.

Every audit finds the same thing: the brand is saying three things and believing one. The site claims innovation, the sales deck claims reliability, and the founder, when you get them talking, cares about craft. The audit names the one and gives the other two a graceful exit.

Skipping the audit does not save the time. It moves it to the middle of the project, when the design is half built and someone senior finally articulates what the company is actually for. Everything built before that sentence gets rebuilt. We have never seen an exception.

The audit ends in a single page: what the brand is, what it is not, and what the site therefore has to feel like. That page is the brief. Everything after it is execution.

## WebGL: when it earns its place and when it is vanity
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_webgl-when-it-earns-its-place.html
Published: 2026-05-06 · Motion

A shader is the most expensive way to render a rectangle. Sometimes the rectangle deserves it.

WebGL is the difference between a site that plays a film and a site that renders one. That distinction is powerful and mostly unnecessary. If a video would do the same job, use the video: it is smaller, it works everywhere, and nobody's laptop fan will spin up.

WebGL earns its place when the reader's input changes the picture in a way a video cannot anticipate: a product that turns to follow the cursor, an image that ripples where you touch it, a field of points that parts as you scroll through it. The moment the picture is interactive, the shader stops being decoration.

It also has to survive contact with the real world. Every WebGL layer we ship has a mobile fallback, disposes its own memory, and stops rendering when it leaves the viewport. A hero that is beautiful on a studio Mac and molten on a two-year-old phone is a failure dressed as an achievement.

The question to ask is not whether the effect is impressive. It is whether the reader would notice if it were gone. If the answer is no, it was vanity, and vanity is the one thing a premium brand cannot afford to be caught doing.

## Typography carries the menu: lessons from a candlelit concept
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_typography-carries-the-menu.html
Published: 2026-04-22 · Concept Notes

On the Nocturne Dining concept there is almost no imagery. What holds the page is type set the way a menu is read.

The brief we set ourselves for Nocturne was unusual: a room too dark to photograph, and a chef who does not want plated shots because the plates change nightly. The site would have to be almost entirely typographic. We took that as a gift.

A menu is read slowly, by candlelight, by someone who wants to be persuaded. We set the type to match: a wide display face for course names, a light body face for descriptions, generous leading, and one hairline between courses. Nothing bold, nothing coloured, nothing that raises its voice.

Motion carries the mood the imagery cannot. Each course reveals line by line as the reader scrolls, the way a waiter describes a dish. The reservation flow lives inside the same rhythm, so booking a table feels like reading to the end of the menu rather than leaving the restaurant to fill in a form.

The lesson we took away: a page does not need a picture to have an atmosphere. It needs a pace, and type sets pace better than anything else on the screen.

## Seamless loops: the craft of ambient video backgrounds
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_seamless-loops.html
Published: 2026-04-08 · AI Visuals

A background loop should be invisible. The moment the reader notices the cut, it has become a distraction.

An ambient loop sits behind type for as long as the reader stays on the page, which can be minutes. Every seam in that loop is a small tap on the shoulder. Five taps and the reader has stopped reading and started watching the video for the cut.

We generate loops at five seconds and hand-select the ones whose first and last frames can be blended without a visible jump. The subject has to be moving slowly enough that the blend is not a stutter, and there must be nothing in the frame with a fixed rhythm, no blinking light, no swinging pendulum, that would reveal the period.

Then we treat the loop like a photograph: one key light, muted saturation, and a scrim so the type in front stays sharp. The loop provides temperature, not information. The best loop is the one nobody could tell you the length of.

Encoding matters as much as content. We ship two sizes, mute the audio track entirely, and preload only the poster frame. A beautiful loop that stalls the page load is a beautiful loop nobody sees.

## Negative space sells: the economics of restraint
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_negative-space-sells.html
Published: 2026-03-25 · Strategy

Empty space on a page looks like waste to a spreadsheet and like confidence to a customer. Only one of them is buying.

Every square inch of a page has a cost, and every stakeholder knows it. So the page fills. Another feature, another badge, another call to action just in case. Each addition is defensible and the sum is a site that looks like it is shouting from behind a market stall.

Premium brands work the other way. A luxury boutique puts one bag on a shelf built for twenty. The empty shelf is the message: we do not need to sell you this. Negative space on a page works the same way. It says the brand is not anxious, and an unanxious brand is one the customer can trust with a premium price.

Restraint is expensive to produce and cheap to recognise. It takes a week of argument to remove the feature grid and a fraction of a second for the visitor to feel the difference. That asymmetry is the entire business case.

The measure we use is simple: if a section were removed, would anyone notice? Every section that fails the test comes out. What remains has room to be looked at, which is the only thing a premium page needs to do.

## From moodboard to motion in three days
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_moodboard-to-motion-three-days.html
Published: 2026-03-11 · Process

The vibe workflow: how a taste-led loop replaces the six-week approval chain without lowering the bar.

The traditional pipeline is a relay race with hand-offs: strategy passes to design, design passes to motion, motion passes to development, and every baton drop takes a week of meetings. The work is not slow. The waiting is.

Our loop keeps strategy, design, motion and code in the same hands for three days. Day one is the moodboard, the single sentence the site has to feel like, and the type and grid that follow from it. Day two is the hero in the browser, moving, and then the first full page. Day three is the client sitting in front of a working site instead of a deck about one.

Speed does not come from cutting steps. It comes from removing the waiting between them. Generated imagery removes the waiting for a shoot. Hand-coded motion removes the waiting for a developer to interpret a designer's video. A client who sees the real thing on day three gives better feedback than one who sees a mock on day forty.

The three days are not the whole project. They are the part that decides whether the project is right. Everything after them is refinement and growth: search, content and testing, which is the part that should take time.

## Industrial brands deserve cinema too
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_industrial-brands-deserve-cinema.html
Published: 2026-02-26 · Concept Notes

Machining, lubricants, steel. The sectors with the most visually extraordinary work are the ones that show it worst.

Walk a machine shop floor and you will see coolant arcs, titanium chips curling off a tool, a spindle finding a tolerance a human eye cannot. Then open the company's site: a stock photo of a handshake, a list of certifications, a phone number.

A foundry at pour is the most cinematic thing in any city. Its website is a PDF. This is not a lack of pride. It is a belief that the customers, engineers and procurement teams, do not respond to beauty. They do. They respond to it more, because they are the only people who can read what the beauty is proving.

On the Axiom Precision concept we opened every capability page on a macro loop of the machine at work. The frames are not decoration; they are evidence. A buyer who watches a surface finish appear under the key light does not need the certification list to believe the tolerance.

The industrial sector is our favourite for exactly this reason. The work is already extraordinary. The studio's job is to point the light at it.

## The preloader is the first scene of the film
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_preloader-first-scene.html
Published: 2026-02-12 · Motion

A loading screen is a second of undivided attention. Most sites spend it on a spinner.

A preloader exists because assets take time, but its real function is dramatic. It is the black frame before the title card. The reader is never more attentive than while waiting for you to begin, and a spinner spends that attention on nothing.

Ours counts from zero to one hundred in the corner while the wordmark rises letter by letter, one letter replaced by a live video slice. Then the whole screen wipes upward and the hero is already moving underneath. The count is honest, it tracks real loading, but the choreography is the point: the site has a rhythm before it has content.

The second visit is different. We remember that the reader has seen the opening and cut it to a beat. A film does not replay its title sequence every time you pause. Neither should a site.

Half a second is not long. It is long enough to tell the reader that everything that follows was composed, not assembled.

## Launching UNLEESH Labs: our public sketchbook
URL: https://unleeshai.com/journal_launching-unleesh-labs.html
Published: 2026-01-28 · Studio

Twenty-five experiments in web motion and generated imagery, published as they are made. Not portfolio pieces. Sketches.

Every studio has a folder of things that never became client work: a shader that did something strange, a product render lit for a direction nobody chose, a loop made at midnight for no reason. We decided to publish ours.

Labs is that folder with a filter bar. Three streams: web motion design, motion image generation, and commercial image generation. Each entry is dated, categorised and shown at full size in a lightbox. Nothing is retouched for the archive; the point is to show the sketch, not the frame.

The portfolio shows what we finished. Labs shows what we are thinking about. It lets a client see where the studio is heading before they brief us, which makes for a better conversation than any capabilities deck.

The archive will grow by a few entries a month. Some will find their way into client sites. Most will stay sketches, which is what a sketchbook is for.
